The "Project changed (…)" rows in the Agent panel come from 21 places. Twenty are notification calls the fork added to OrcaSlicer files. The last one is a JusPrin listener that fires when slicing starts, finishes, or becomes invalid. The word in parentheses lists which of seven reason flags were set, joined with "+".

## The seven reason flags

Orca-side flags are defined in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp:16`. [OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:46](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:46) maps them to JusPrin's names:

| Orca flag | JusPrin flag | Shown in timeline as |
|---|---|---|
| Selection | Selection | never creates a row |
| Objects | Contents | `contents` |
| History | History | `history` |
| Transform | Transform | `transform` |
| Plates | Plates | `plates` |
| Project | Project | never creates a row (a new or reset project starts a new timeline instead) |
| Settings | Settings | never creates a row |

A timeline row is only recorded when the change includes `contents`, `transform` or `plates` ([ProjectPersistence.cpp:82](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:82)). `history` only appears added to one of those. One more rule: every notification also gets `History` added whenever undo or redo becomes available or unavailable ([PlaterProjectState.cpp:36](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/PlaterProjectState.cpp:36)).

## What the rows in your screenshot probably are

This is my reading of the code. I did not reproduce your session.

- **`(plates)` alone** can only come from the last row, the slice listener. Every Orca plate call above also passes `History`. So those rows are slicing starting, finishing, or being invalidated, not edits you made. The "— current" row at the bottom is almost certainly the slice that produced the ~16 min estimate.
- **`(contents+plates+history)`**: objects were added or removed, for example loading the cube.
- **`(plates+history)`**: a plate was added, deleted, switched to, or reordered.

This means slicing adds rows to the undo timeline (and a Revert checkpoint to each) even though the model didn't change. The comment at [OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:178](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:178) already worries about this: publishing for nothing "would advance the revision — and add a history entry". If you want, I can stop slice-only changes from creating timeline rows.
what are the flags mean? use plain english

Each flag says roughly what kind of thing just changed in the open project. OrcaSlicer can set several at once, and the timeline joins them with "+", so `contents+plates+history` means three kinds of change happened together.

- **Selection**: what you have selected changed, such as clicking a different object. The model itself stays the same, so this never adds a timeline row.
- **Contents** (called "Objects" inside Orca): the set of objects changed. One was added, deleted, duplicated, split or renamed.
- **Transform**: an object was moved, rotated or scaled.
- **Plates**: something about the build plates changed. It covers several unrelated things:
  - a plate was added, deleted or reordered
  - a different plate became the active one
  - which plate an object sits on changed
  - slicing started, finished, or its result was thrown away because something changed
- **History**: the undo/redo list changed. Usually a new undo step was recorded, or undo or redo just became available or unavailable. It's a side effect of other changes, not a change of its own.
- **Project**: a different project is now open, such as File → New or opening a file. Instead of adding a row, this starts a fresh timeline.
- **Settings**: a print, filament or printer setting changed, such as layer height. This doesn't add a timeline row today.

Only **contents**, **transform** and **plates** add a row to the timeline. The other flags are shown only when they arrive together with one of those three.

That's why "plates" is the confusing one in your screenshot. A row that says only `(plates)` usually means slicing started or finished, not that you touched a plate.

content.text:
For moves, rotations and scaling, yes. For plates, no. The one plate change with no undo step is slicing.

**Transform (move, rotate, scale):** Orca always records an undo step for these. The only place that sends Transform passes History with it every time ([Plater.cpp:5172](src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:5172)).

**Plates:** it depends on the cause.
- **Plate edits you make**, like adding, deleting, switching or reordering plates, do record an undo step. For example, `take_snapshot("add partplate")` at [Plater.cpp:10142](src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:10142) and `take_snapshot("select partplate!")` at [Plater.cpp:17668](src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:17668). Those calls send Plates and History together.
- **Slicing starting, finishing or being thrown away** also sends Plates, but it isn't an undo step, so History isn't set ([OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:197](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:197)). That's why some rows in your screenshot say only `(plates)`.

The reverse doesn't hold either. History can arrive without Transform or Plates, for example when Orca records an undo step for a change that none of the other flags describe.

In the row labels, History adds almost nothing. When it appears next to contents, transform or plates, it just repeats "this was an undo-able edit." The label code ([ProjectPersistence.cpp:100](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:100)) could leave it out. Its only other use is the Agent's approval check ([ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:23](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:23)). That check treats any project change as a reason to re-check an Agent action that's waiting for approval.

**What "timeline" means:** the list of "Project start" and "Project changed (…)" rows in the Agent panel in your screenshot. Each row is a saved copy of the project taken right after a change, and "Revert here" puts the project back to that copy. The code calls these "revisions". They're stored with the project by [ProjectPersistence.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp), separately from Orca's own undo list.
Do a systematic analysis to see to come up with a proposal for a clean design that decide what event should go into the timeline, and give me your rationale behind it in plain English. Upper style.

# A cleaner rule for what goes into the Agent panel's revision timeline

**Proposal:** only create a timeline row when the inputs to the printed result actually changed. Answer that from two sources Orca already maintains: its undo list, plus a small fingerprint of the few print inputs the undo list doesn't cover. Stop inferring it from the change notifications the fork added to OrcaSlicer. Those notifications are the cause of both problems in your screenshot: they record noise (slicing, switching plates) and miss most real edits (mirror, painting, arrange, per-object settings, and more).

## What the timeline is supposed to hold

The spec already defines this ([agent-webview-bridge-handoff.md:271](agent-docs/jusprin/agent-webview-bridge-handoff.md:271)):

> Create a revision after each completed manufacturing change.

It lists geometry, transforms, plates, arrangement, modifiers, painting, settings and custom G-code as manufacturing changes. It lists messages, camera, selection and renaming as not. Slicing is a separate record the spec calls a "build".

Each row costs about 170 ms (the checkpoint is a full project file export) and about 31 KB on disk. "Revert here" permanently deletes everything after the row, including chat messages. So every noise row is a destructive button that means nothing, and every missing row is a point you can't go back to.

## What it holds today

**Noise: rows that aren't changes**
- Slicing starting, finishing, or its result being thrown away creates a `(plates)` row.
- Switching the active plate creates a `(plates+history)` row. "Slice all" switches plates itself, so one click can add several rows.

**Gaps: real edits that create no row**

I had a subagent trace about 30 kinds of edits through the code. I spot-checked mirror and arrange myself. These reach no notification that creates a row:
- Transforms: mirror, arrange, orient, fill bed, moving the wipe tower
- Painting: supports, seams, color, fuzzy skin, brim ears
- Parts: adding a modifier or part, changing a part's type, split to parts
- Per-object settings: settings overrides, filament assignment, layer ranges, variable layer height
- Plates: the plate settings dialog (bed type, print order), locking a plate
- Other: custom G-code from the preview slider, text/emboss/SVG, adding a primitive, toggling printable, reload from disk
- Print, filament and printer settings (by design today)

Many of these do produce a row by accident. If the plate had been sliced, the edit throws the slice away, and that shows up as `(plates)`. On an unsliced plate the edit leaves no row at all.

**Labels:** `contents+plates+history` describes which code ran, not what you did.

## Why patching the flags won't fix it

The decision rests on about 20 notification calls placed by hand in OrcaSlicer code. They answer "which code path ran", not "did the print's inputs change". Closing the gaps would mean adding calls in 20 or more more places in Orca files. Each one is another rebase conflict for the fork, and every future Orca feature would silently become a new gap.

## The proposal

**1. Decide from state, not from events.** A row is created when either of these is true:
- **Orca recorded a real undo step since the last row.** Orca already defines "real" in `src/slic3r/Utils/UndoRedo.hpp:100`: an Action or tool-action undo step whose name doesn't end in "!". Orca names selection steps and plate switching with a trailing "!" (`"select partplate!"`), and slicing never records an undo step. Orca uses this same rule for its unsaved-changes asterisk and auto-backup, so it's maintained upstream. It covers every undo-able edit in the gap list, including undo and redo themselves.
- **The inputs Orca keeps outside the undo list changed.** These are the print/filament/printer settings in force (including unsaved edits), the per-plate settings, and the per-plate custom G-code. A small fingerprint of these, compared with the last row's, covers settings, the plate settings dialog and the preview slider.

**2. Check at a quiet moment, not inside each event.** Run the check when the app goes idle after activity, so a burst of changes gives one row. Don't check while a tool like paint or cut is open, or while a background job like arrange is running. When the tool closes or the job ends, one row captures the whole session. This mirrors how Orca already merges a painting session into one undo step.

**3. Labels come from Orca's undo-step names.** Examples: "Move Object", "Arrange", "Variable layer height - Smooth all". A few are internal names ("select_arrange partplate", "smooth_mesh") and need a small table of friendlier names. Settings rows use the setting's own label, which the adapter already computes for the "N changes from preset" line on the setup card.

**4. Where the code lives.** The check goes in `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter`, which is JusPrin code. It publishes one new change reason, "manufacturing change", together with the label. `ProjectPersistence` creates a row only when it sees that reason. The flag-joining code (`kManufacturingReasons`, `cause_of`) is deleted.

It needs no OrcaSlicer file changes. Plater already exposes `undo_redo_stack_main()` (Plater.hpp:597), and the gizmo state is readable through `canvas3D()`. The existing 20 notification calls stay, because the Agent page's live context still depends on them.

## What you'd see

| Action | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Move, rotate or scale | row | row |
| Mirror, arrange, paint, add modifier | usually no row | row (painting: one per session) |
| Change layer height | row only if the plate was sliced | row |
| Slice, or slice all | one or more rows | no row |
| Switch plate, select object | row / no row | no row |
| Undo | row | row, labeled with what was undone |

## Alternatives I rejected

- **Add the missing notification calls and split "plates" into plate layout vs active plate.** This is the fork-maintenance cost described above, and it never stays complete.
- **Use the slicer's own "did the inputs change" answer (`background_process.apply()`).** It only examines the plate currently being sliced, so edits on other plates are invisible.
- **Compare full project exports.** At about 170 ms each, that's fine for saving a checkpoint but too slow to run as the "did anything change" check.

## Related problem, same cause

The Agent's approval-staleness check ([ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:22](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:22)) relies on the same notifications. If you approve an Agent proposal after mirroring or painting, it won't be flagged as out of date. The new "manufacturing change" reason could feed that check too.

## Open questions for you

1. **Renames.** Orca treats renaming an object or plate as an edit; the spec says renaming creates no row. I'd follow the spec and filter renames out, unless object names matter to the printer. I haven't checked whether they end up in the G-code.
2. **Settings edits in a row.** Should several settings changes with nothing else in between merge into one row? I'd merge them, so tuning five settings doesn't add five Revert buttons.
3. **Unverified:** whether increasing or decreasing instance counts records an undo step. If it doesn't, it goes into the fingerprint too.

If you agree, I'd test it with unit tests on the fake workspace, plus a scenario in the existing shell test harness (the app driven without a person) that runs mirror, a painting session, slice-all, plate switching and a settings change.

I can also turn this into a shareable page if you want to circulate it.

**Recording raw events and merging them only in the UI is a good design for the list of changes. It doesn't work for the saved copies that "Revert here" restores**, so the proposal below splits those two things. Also, I got the renaming question wrong last time: the spec only exempts renaming the *project*, and object renames were never carved out.

## Correction on renaming

The spec ([agent-webview-bridge-handoff.md:271](agent-docs/jusprin/agent-webview-bridge-handoff.md:271)) lists "project renaming" as not creating a revision. Renaming the project changes no object, plate or setting, so it belongs with camera movement: not a change to the print. It isn't a special case. The spec says nothing about object or plate renames. Under the proposal below they're recorded like any other edit, with no exception.

I'd still rewrite that spec paragraph as a single rule instead of a list of exclusions. That drops "project renaming" along with the rest of the list.

## Where raw events plus UI merging works, and where it doesn't

It works for the **list of changes**. Each entry is a few bytes: time, kind, label. Writing every change as it happens means no merging logic in the recorder and no "is the user finished yet" timing. No information is lost. The UI can merge in whatever way reads best, and you can change the merge rule later without touching saved data. You're right that this avoids the messy part.

It breaks down if **every raw event also gets its own restorable copy**. Today each timeline row is a full project export, meshes included (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:390` uses the same settings as a normal save), and takes about 170 ms. Some edits produce a lot of raw events. Painting records one undo step per brush stroke (`GLGizmoPainterBase.cpp:968`, on mouse-up). A painting session of 200 strokes on a 20 MB model would mean 200 exports: about 34 seconds of UI freezes and about 4 GB of copies. So the list can be raw, but restorable copies have to be rarer.

## New proposal

**1. A raw change log, written as it happens.** Every change to the print gets one entry. Two sources supply them:
- **Orca's undo list.** Every new real undo step becomes an entry labeled with Orca's name for it ("Move Object", "Arrange", "Paint-on supports"). Undo and redo are entries too. "Real" means Orca's own rule (`UndoRedo.hpp:100`). That rule excludes selection and plate switching, and slicing never records an undo step. This isn't merging, just a yes/no test on each event on its own.
- **Settings changes.** Each committed settings change becomes an entry labeled with the setting's name. The plate settings dialog and the preview slider's custom G-code record no undo step and send no notification today. Each needs a one-line notification call added in OrcaSlicer's Plater.cpp (`Plater.cpp:17968` and `:5270`, both already call `set_plater_dirty`). Those two lines are the only OrcaSlicer changes.

Slicing, selection, switching plates and camera movement never enter the log.

**2. Restorable copies taken at conversation boundaries.** When anything is added to the conversation (your message, an Agent reply, an Agent tool call) and the log has entries since the last copy, take one copy first.

Every trigger is a definite moment, so there are no timing guesses. Your manual edits between two messages share one copy. That's what "Revert here" in a conversation needs anyway. Step-by-step undo within a stretch of editing is still Orca's own Undo.

**3. The UI merges.** It shows each run of log entries between two conversation items as one group, for example "Moved object, painted supports (14 strokes), changed layer height". Each group has one Revert button that restores its copy. The rule to keep in sync: **every group the UI shows must end at a copy**. Merging "everything between two conversation items" satisfies it automatically.

## What changes from today

| Action | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Mirror, arrange, paint, modifiers, per-object settings | usually no row | logged; revertible at the next conversation item |
| A painting session | nothing, or one accidental row | one log entry per stroke, shown as one group |
| Settings, plate settings, slider custom G-code | row only if the plate was sliced | logged |
| Slice, slice all, switch plate, select | noise rows | not logged |
| Many edits with no chat in between | one expensive copy each (when they create a row at all) | one copy |

## What gets simpler in the code

- The flag-joining code in `ProjectPersistence` goes away: `kManufacturingReasons` and `cause_of` at [ProjectPersistence.cpp:82](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:82).
- There's no "quiet time" logic. The recorder reacts only to definite events: a new undo step, a settings change, a new conversation item.
- The two stored record types map directly to what they are: log entries (cheap, many) and copies (expensive, few).

## Two things to know

- **Revert granularity gets coarser.** You can't revert to a point between two manual edits unless a conversation item sits between them. I think that's the right trade: Orca's Undo already handles fine-grained steps, and "Revert here" is about going back in the conversation. If you do want in-between revert points, the copy trigger is the one knob to turn. It doesn't affect the log.
- **Unhandled edge case:** if you send a message while an arrange job is still running, the copy is taken before the arrangement lands. The fix is to have the copy wait for the running job. It's small, but a real case to cover in tests.

Apart from the two lines in OrcaSlicer's Plater.cpp, the changes stay in JusPrin code: the workspace adapter and `ProjectPersistence` on the C++ side, and the revision group component in the Agent page. If this matches what you want, I'll write it up as the spec change first (the rewritten revisions paragraph), then implement.

# Handoff: what goes into the Agent panel's revision timeline

Written 2026-09-10 on branch `jusprin-newui` at commit `82256c8092`. This file
is deliberately not committed. Line numbers below are from that commit; re-find
them by the quoted names if the code has moved.

## Summary

The Agent panel shows a timeline of "Project start" / "Project changed (…)"
rows, each with a "Revert here" button. Today the rows are decided by change
notifications scattered through OrcaSlicer code, which record noise (slicing,
switching plates) and miss most real edits (mirror, painting, arrange,
modifiers, per-object settings, custom G-code, plate settings). The decision,
agreed with Kenneth: record every real change raw and cheaply in a change log,
take restorable copies only at conversation boundaries, and let the Agent page
merge consecutive changes for display. This document explains the goal, each
decision, why, what was rejected, and how to build and test it.

## Terms used in this document

- **Timeline**: the list of rows in the Agent panel between chat messages. Each
  row today is a *revision* in the code (`RevisionInfo`,
  `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.hpp:38`).
- **Copy** (today called a revision checkpoint or snapshot): a full project
  file, meshes included, exported so the project can be restored to that point.
  Written by `ProjectPersistence::capture_revision`
  (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:303`) using
  `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::export_project_archive`
  (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:378`), which uses
  the same save strategy as an ordinary project save.
- **Change log entry**: new in this design. A small record (time, kind, label)
  of one change to the print's inputs. No project data.
- **Undo step**: one entry on OrcaSlicer's own undo stack
  (`src/slic3r/Utils/UndoRedo.hpp`).
- **Revert here**: restores a copy and permanently deletes everything recorded
  after it, in every conversation — later messages, approvals, builds, and
  copies. Spec: `agent-docs/jusprin/agent-webview-bridge-handoff.md:282`.

## Goal

A person reading the Agent panel should see one truthful history of how the
print's inputs changed, in step with the conversation, and be able to go back
to any point where the conversation moved on. Concretely:

1. Every change to an input of the printed result is recorded — geometry,
   transforms, arrangement, plates, modifiers, painting, per-object and global
   settings, custom G-code, filament mapping, names. No hand-picked exceptions.
2. Things that are not inputs are never recorded: slicing (already recorded
   separately as builds), selection, switching the active plate, camera.
3. Recording is cheap enough that a 200-stroke painting session does not freeze
   the app or fill the disk.
4. The rule for what counts as a change does not depend on the fork adding a
   notification call to every OrcaSlicer feature, because that list is never
   complete and every call is a future rebase conflict.

## Why the current implementation fails the goal

### How it works today

1. The fork added about 20 `Plater::notify_project_state_changed(reasons)` calls
   to OrcaSlicer code. Reasons are flags: Selection, Objects, History,
   Transform, Plates, Project, Settings
   (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp:16`).
2. `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter` maps them to `WorkspaceChangeReasons`
   (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:46`) and also publishes `Plates` whenever any
   plate's slice state changes (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:174-198`).
3. `ProjectPersistence::on_workspace_changed`
   (`ProjectPersistence.cpp:142`) writes a copy synchronously whenever the
   reasons include Contents, Transform or Plates (`kManufacturingReasons`,
   `ProjectPersistence.cpp:82`), labeled by joining flag names (`cause_of`,
   `ProjectPersistence.cpp:86`) — hence rows like
   `Project changed (contents+plates+history)`.

### Problem 1: noise

- Slicing starting, finishing, or its result being thrown away creates a
  `(plates)` row, via the slice watcher above.
- Switching the active plate creates a `(plates+history)` row
  (`src/slic3r/GUI/PartPlate.cpp:4803`). "Slice all" switches plates itself
  (`Plater.cpp:10101`, `Plater.cpp:10209`), so one click adds several rows.
- Each row costs a full project export: about 170 ms on the UI thread and about
  31 KB, measured on a small two-plate test project during Phase 4. Real
  projects with real meshes are far larger, since the copy contains the meshes.

### Problem 2: gaps

A code trace of about 30 edit types found that these reach no notification
that creates a row. Mirror and arrange were re-verified by hand; the rest come
from the trace, with file references kept in the appendix.

- Mirror, arrange, orient, fill bed, moving the wipe tower.
- All painting: supports, seams, color, fuzzy skin, brim ears.
- Adding a modifier, negative volume or support blocker; changing a part's
  type; split to parts; text, emboss, SVG; adding a primitive; reload from disk;
  toggling printable.
- Per-object setting overrides, per-object filament assignment, layer ranges,
  variable layer height.
- The plate settings dialog (bed type, print order, layer sequences), plate
  lock, filament mapping.
- Custom G-code, color changes and pauses set from the preview layer slider.
- Print, filament and printer settings (excluded on purpose today).

Many of these create a row only by accident: if the plate had been sliced, the
edit throws the slice away and the slice watcher reports `(plates)`. On an
unsliced plate nothing is recorded at all.

### Problem 3: labels

`contents+plates+history` says which code paths ran, not what the person did.

### Root cause

The decision "did the print's inputs change?" is inferred from which
hand-placed notification fired. Those calls describe code paths, not state.
Closing the gaps this way means 20 or more new calls in OrcaSlicer files, and
every future OrcaSlicer feature silently becomes a new gap.

## Decisions

### D1. Two record types: a cheap change log and rare restorable copies

Every change goes into a change log as a small entry. Restorable copies are a
separate, rarer record.

**Why.** Kenneth's direction was to save raw change events as they happen and
let the UI merge them for display, which removes any merging or "has the person
finished?" logic from the recorder. That is right for the log. It cannot apply
to copies, because some edits produce many raw events: painting records one
undo step per brush stroke (`src/slic3r/GUI/Gizmos/GLGizmoPainterBase.cpp:968`,
on mouse-up). A 200-stroke session on a 20 MB model would mean 200 exports —
roughly 34 seconds of UI freezes and about 4 GB of copies. So the log is raw
and complete, and copies are taken at a coarser, well-defined moment (D4).

### D2. What counts as a change

A change log entry is written for each of these, and nothing else:

1. **A new real undo step on OrcaSlicer's undo stack.** "Real" is OrcaSlicer's
   own rule, `snapshot_modifies_project` (`src/slic3r/Utils/UndoRedo.hpp:95-103`):
   the step's type is Action, GizmoAction or ProjectSeparator, and its name does
   not end in "!". OrcaSlicer names selection steps (`"Selection-Add!"` and
   similar) and plate switching (`"select partplate!"`, `Plater.cpp:17668`) with
   a trailing "!", and slicing never records an undo step. OrcaSlicer uses this
   same rule for its unsaved-changes asterisk and its auto-backup
   (`Plater::priv::up_to_date`, `Plater.cpp:11757`), so upstream maintains it.
   Undo and redo also produce entries (the active position on the undo stack
   moves).
2. **A settings change.** Print, filament and printer settings are not on the
   undo stack. `Plater::on_config_change` already notifies with `Settings`
   (`Plater.cpp:16922`); that becomes a change log entry naming the setting(s).
3. **An edit that marks the project dirty without an undo step.** See D7. These
   are custom G-code from the preview slider, the plate settings dialog,
   filament mapping and brim ears.

Renames of objects and plates are recorded like any other undo step. There is
no rename exception.

**Why.** This rule is defined by state OrcaSlicer already keeps, not by which
code path ran, so a new OrcaSlicer feature that records undo steps is covered
automatically. It removes all the noise in Problem 1 by construction and covers
every undo-able edit in Problem 2.

### D3. Record raw; merge only in the Agent page

The recorder writes one entry per change with no merging, deduplication or
delay. The Agent page groups consecutive entries for display.

**Why.** Merging while recording needs timing guesses: is a tool still open, is
a job still running, has the person paused. Those guesses are where the
complexity and the bugs live. Merging at display time loses no information, and
the merge rule can change later without touching saved data.

### D4. Take a restorable copy at conversation boundaries

Just before anything is added to the conversation — a person's message, an
Agent reply, an Agent tool activity record — take one copy if the change log
has entries since the last copy. Otherwise take none.

**Why.** Every trigger is a definite moment, so the recorder never guesses. It
matches what "Revert here" is for: going back to a point in the conversation.
Step-by-step undo within a stretch of manual editing remains OrcaSlicer's own
Undo. Agent changes stay individually revertible, because an Agent change is
bracketed by conversation items (the tool activity record before it, the reply
after it).

**Accepted cost.** You cannot revert to a point between two manual edits unless
a conversation item sits between them. Kenneth accepted this. If finer revert
points are ever wanted, the copy trigger is the only thing to change; the log
is unaffected.

**Edge case to handle.** If a message is sent while an OrcaSlicer background job
that edits the model is still running (arrange, orient, fill bed), a copy taken
immediately would miss the job's result. The copy should wait for the job to
finish. Find the Plater's job-worker idle check when implementing; it was not
looked up for this handoff.

### D5. How the Agent page groups entries

The page shows each run of change log entries between two conversation items
as one group, for example "Moved object, painted supports (14 strokes), changed
layer height". The group carries one "Revert here" button, which restores the
copy taken at the end of that group.

**Invariant:** every group the page shows must end at a copy. Grouping by
"everything between two conversation items" satisfies this automatically,
because D4 takes a copy at exactly those boundaries. The newest group, after
the last conversation item, has no copy yet: it is the live project and shows
as current, with no Revert button.

### D6. Labels come from OrcaSlicer's names

- Undo steps: the step's own name, e.g. "Move Object", "Arrange", "Variable
  layer height - Smooth all". Some names are internal ("select_arrange
  partplate", "smooth_mesh", "MoveInMeasure"); map those to readable text with a
  small table in JusPrin code. Some names are translated with `_u8L` and some
  are not; decide whether to store the raw name and translate at display time.
- Undo and redo: "Undo: <name>" / "Redo: <name>".
- Settings: the setting's label from its definition, the way
  `preset_deltas_of` does it (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:112`). Switching a whole
  preset changes many keys at once; label it as a preset switch rather than
  listing every key.

**Why.** These are the names people already see in OrcaSlicer's own Undo menu.

### D7. OrcaSlicer footprint: one hook in `set_plater_dirty`

The edits in D2 item 3 record no undo step and send no notification, but all of
them call `Plater::set_plater_dirty(true)`. The preferred fix is one additive
line: have `Plater::priv::set_plater_dirty` (`Plater.cpp:4444`) call
`notify_project_state_changed(...)` when `is_dirty` is true. Its callers:

| Caller | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Plater.cpp:5270` | custom G-code / color change / pause from the preview slider |
| `Plater.cpp:17976` | bed type in the plate settings dialog |
| `Plater.cpp:18008` | the plate settings dialog's other fields (appears to; confirm) |
| `Plater.cpp:18070` | filament-to-extruder mapping for a plate |
| `GLGizmoBrimEars.cpp:862` | brim ears |
| `Auxiliary.cpp:513` | setting the project cover image — not a print input (open question) |

Which reason flag the hook sends is the implementer's call. It needs to be
distinguishable enough that the adapter can write a sensible label; a new
neutral flag is acceptable.

**Why one hook instead of a call at each site:** fork-stewardship principle 5,
"one seam beats many touch points" (`agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md:57`).
One line inside an existing function is one conflict draw at rebase instead of
five. It is also additive and product-neutral. The rest of the design uses
public Plater API only: `undo_redo_stack_main()` (`Plater.hpp:597`), and the
stack's `snapshots()` and `active_snapshot_time()` (`UndoRedo.hpp:162`, `:168`).

### D8. Spec change

Rewrite the paragraph at
`agent-docs/jusprin/agent-webview-bridge-handoff.md:271-275`. It currently lists
exclusions, including "project renaming", with no rationale. Replace the list
with the rule. Suggested text:

> Record every change to an input of the manufactured result as a change log
> entry when it happens: geometry, transforms, plates, arrangement, modifiers,
> painted surfaces, names, printer/process/material settings, custom G-code,
> and any other input. Slicing is recorded as a build, not as a change.
> Selection, the active plate, camera, messages and drafts are not inputs and
> are not recorded. A restorable revision is taken whenever a conversation
> item is added and changes exist since the previous revision. The Agent panel
> shows the changes between two conversation items as one group whose Revert
> here restores the revision that ends the group.

Also update the Phase 4 section of the same file if it restates the old rule.

## Alternatives considered and rejected

- **Add the missing notification calls to OrcaSlicer and split "Plates" into
  plate layout versus active plate.** 20+ more touch points in OrcaSlicer files,
  each a rebase conflict, and still incomplete for every future feature.
- **A copy per raw event.** Too slow and too large for painting sessions (D1).
- **Merge while recording, capturing a copy at "quiet time" (idle, no tool
  open, no job running).** This was the previous proposal. It works, but the
  timing rules are exactly the fragile, synchronous merging that D3 removes.
- **Use the slicer's own "did the inputs change" answer**
  (`background_process.apply()`, `Plater.cpp:7992-8003`). It only examines the
  plate currently being sliced, so edits on other plates are invisible.
- **Compare full project exports to detect change.** About 170 ms each; fine
  for taking a copy, too slow as a change detector.
- **Reuse `manufacturing_input_hash`**
  (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ManufacturingHistory.cpp:25`). It covers only
  preset names and object transforms, not painting, modifiers, process
  settings or custom G-code. It also deliberately ignores object names. It
  serves build staleness and should stay as is.

## Implementation guide

### 1. Workspace contract (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp`)

- The contract must stay free of wxWidgets and OrcaSlicer types
  (`agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:75-85`).
- A change log entry needs a kind and a label; today `WorkspaceChanged` carries
  only reasons and a revision number (`Workspace.hpp:247`). Add what is needed,
  e.g. a list of edits on the change, or a separate subscription. Your design
  choice.
- `WorkspaceChangeDelivery::commit` drops a change whose reasons are None
  (`Workspace.hpp:340`). The notification fired from `take_snapshot`
  (`Plater.cpp:11716`) carries None, so undo-step detection must happen in the
  adapter, which sees every `ProjectStateChanged`, not in persistence.
- Update `FakeWorkspace` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/FakeWorkspace.hpp`)
  so tests can simulate undo steps, "!" steps, undo/redo, settings changes and
  slice-state changes.

### 2. Adapter (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`)

- On every `ProjectStateChanged` (`on_project_state_changed`, line 472),
  compare the undo stack with what was last seen. Track by snapshot
  **timestamp**, not index: `release_least_recently_used` drops old snapshots,
  and a ProjectSeparator (new or opened project) clears the stack
  (`Plater.cpp:11693`).
- New snapshots after the last seen timestamp that pass
  `snapshot_modifies_project` become entries. Ignore the uncaptured placeholder
  that may be the active snapshot (comment at `UndoRedo.hpp:165-167`).
- `take_snapshot` runs *before* the action modifies the model, so the entry is
  written at the start of the action. That is fine for the log. Copies happen
  later, at conversation boundaries.
- If the active snapshot time moves without a new snapshot, that is undo or
  redo. Write an "Undo: …" or "Redo: …" entry.
- Settings: on a `Settings` notification, find which keys changed by diffing
  the configuration in force against the last seen one, and write an entry.
  Note from the trace: settings notifications are skipped while
  `inside_snapshot_capture()` is true.
- Slice-state changes (`on_slice_status_changed`) keep publishing for the
  Agent page's live context but must never produce an entry.

### 3. OrcaSlicer hook

The one line from D7. Follow `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` and
record its "Before you finish" evidence (lines 117-133): the `git merge-tree`
rebase simulation with both endpoint commits, an account of any upstream line
touched, and what the fork now owns.

### 4. Persistence (`ProjectPersistence.cpp`, `ProjectStateDocument.cpp`)

- Add the change log to `state.json` as a new array whose entries carry the
  document's global `seq`. Revert already truncates everything with a later
  `seq` (`ProjectStateDocument::revert_to_revision`, around
  `ProjectStateDocument.cpp:1002`); extend it to the change log.
- Replace the capture trigger. Delete `kManufacturingReasons` and `cause_of`.
  Take a copy only at conversation boundaries (D4). Conversation items are
  appended in `AgentHost.cpp` at lines 539 (`upsert_activity`), 934, 1093,
  1535, 1547 and 1813 (`append_message`). Route them through one choke point
  rather than adding a call at each site.
- Keep the initial copy at project start, including its retry logic
  (`retry_initial_capture`, `ProjectPersistence.cpp:280`); the canvas cannot
  export before GL is ready.
- Keep the `m_in_revert` guard so restoring a copy does not log the restore as
  a stream of changes.
- **Compatibility.** `state.json` is at `kSchemaVersion = 2`
  (`ProjectStateDocument.hpp:80`). Loading merges older documents onto a fresh
  skeleton (`ProjectStateDocument.cpp:383-405`), so a document without a change
  log loads with an empty one. Existing revisions must stay revertible and keep
  showing their stored `cause` text. Bump the schema version only if an older
  build reading the new file would lose meaning; ask Kenneth whether any
  `state.json` has shipped before deciding.

### 5. Bridge and Agent page

- `RevisionInfo` (`AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts:288`, serialized by
  `revision_json` in `AgentHost.cpp:128`) stays as the copy record. Add change
  log entries to the state payload. This is additive: advertise it in the
  capabilities list, not with a protocol version bump.
- `MessageList.tsx:65` places markers after messages by `afterMessageId`.
  Replace the per-revision marker with a group per D5.
  `RevisionMarker.tsx:20` builds today's "Project changed (…)" label.
- Keep the existing destructive-confirmation flow on Revert.
- Rebuild the Agent page bundle after changing it (see
  `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` and the design system rules in
  `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` before any UI change).

## Tests

Update:

- `tests/agent/test_project_state.cpp:498` "manufacturing changes capture
  revisions; selection does not" — rewrite for the new rule (a rename logs a
  change; a copy appears only at a conversation boundary).
- Revert tests in the same file (lines 388-900) — extend them to cover change
  log truncation.

Add, at minimum:

- Selection, a "!" undo step, plate switching, slice start/finish/invalidate:
  no entries.
- A painting-like burst of N undo steps: N entries, and one copy at the next
  conversation item.
- A settings change: one entry, labeled with the setting.
- Undo and redo: entries, labeled.
- No changes between two conversation items: no copy.
- A legacy v2 `state.json` with old-style revisions: loads, displays, reverts.
- Page tests (Vitest): grouping between messages, one Revert per group, no
  Revert on the live group. Per the "prove guard tests fail first" lesson, break
  the grouping on purpose once and watch the test fail.
- Real-app checks with the workspace harness (`tests/workspace/`) and the shell
  harness (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`, see
  `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`): mirror, a painting session,
  slice all, plate switching, a settings change, custom G-code from the slider,
  and the plate settings dialog, each checked against the expected entries and
  copies.

Build and test commands are in `AGENTS.md`.

## Open questions

1. Should setting the project cover image (`Auxiliary.cpp:513`) produce a change
   log entry? It is project content but not a print input. Recommendation: no.
   Filter it in the adapter or leave that caller unhooked. Confirm with
   Kenneth.
2. Schema version bump for `state.json`: see Implementation guide section 4.
3. Instance-count changes (increase/decrease instances): Kenneth asked to leave
   these for now. The trace found they send only Selection. Whether they record
   an undo step was not checked.

## Related issue, out of scope

The Agent's approval-staleness check (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:22`) uses
the same notification flags, so an approval given after a mirror or a painting
stroke is not flagged as stale. The new change detection could feed that check
later. Do not change it as part of this work without asking.

It covers the goal, eight numbered decisions each with its reasoning, the rejected alternatives, an implementation guide with file and line pointers, the tests to add, and an appendix of which edits reach a change notification today.

While writing it I found three things that change or sharpen what I told you before:

- **One line in OrcaSlicer instead of two.** The edits that record no undo step all call one function, `Plater::set_plater_dirty(true)`. They are custom G-code from the preview slider, the plate settings dialog, filament mapping, and brim ears. Adding the notification inside that function covers all four with a single additive line in Plater.cpp. The fork-stewardship doc prefers that over several separate edits. Filament mapping and brim ears were gaps I hadn't accounted for.
- **One open question for you.** Setting the project cover image also calls that function. It changes the project but isn't a print input. I recommended not logging it, and the handoff asks the next agent to confirm with you.
- **The existing "manufacturing hash" can't be reused.** The code that tracks whether a slice is out of date already has a fingerprint. It covers only preset names and object positions, and it deliberately ignores object names. The handoff tells the next agent to leave it alone.

- ask you whether any saved Agent state has shipped before bumping its file-format version;
